recipes.name: Lemon Chicken with Broccoli
ingredients_raw: 2 packets Swanson® Flavor Boost™ Concentrated Chicken Broth

steps.text: Grate 1 tablespoon zest and squeeze 1/4 cup juice from the lemon.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until well browned on all sides. Remove the chicken from the skillet. Pour off any fat.

Reduce the heat to medium. Heat the remaining oil in the skillet. Add the onion and garlic and cook and stir for 2 minutes. Stir in the concentrated broth and lemon juice. Return the chicken to the skillet. Reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the broccoli and lemon zest in the skillet. Cover and cook until the broccoli is tender-crisp.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Chicken with Broccoli
raw_recipe.description: Sauteed chicken and tender-crisp broccoli are infused with flavor from a savory lemon sauce in this exquisite skillet dish.

review.reviewBody: Cooked according to recipe but used different brand of broth. Turned out amazing! Will definitely cook again!

Absolutely love this recipe with a few changes that I gathered from other reviews! I made a thicker sauce by adding self rising flour, more lemon juice, honey, water and some sugar to calm the strong lemon flavor. I also seasoned my chicken with lemon pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, garlic salt and rosemary. Very flavorful and yummy!

Easy to make, Tastes great. I sprinkled some garlic & herb seasoning on the chicken when I browned it. I did not find this dish salty at all like others did. I also used asparagus instead of broccoli and I put the asparagus in with the chicken and ended up cooking the dish covered on low for 40 minutes. The chicken was very tender.

Much the same can be done with using spinach rather than the broccoli, but in either case I de-glazed the pan with some white wine and also added some sautéed mushrooms to the dish. Excellent served over brown rice.
tasty and easy to make. I only used one packet of concentrated chicken broth (to cut down on the salt) and as I browned the chicken I sprinkled salt-free Lemon Pepper seasoning on the chicken.

Maybe I just didn't brown the chicken enough, or maybe it's because I just used thighs, but even after I browned it and poured off the fat, it still felt greasy. 

Because one of the comments said there wasn't enough sauce, I added a little bottle (like, 4 ounces) of white wine after cooking the chicken, to deglaze the pan, to the onions and garlic, and that made more sauce. Also used organic low sodium chicken stock instead of the concentrate. 

Don't think I'll try it again, or if I do, it'll be with chicken breasts instead of thighs.
Perfection. I subbed asparagus for the broc & added lemon zest. Then used cornstarch to thicken the sauce. My mouth was happy!
This was very good. I used chicken thighs. Also used 3 flavor packets instead of 2 and added some water as I wanted more sauce. Really enjoyed the sauce over rice! Will make this again.
I used 2 cups of chicken stock instead of the Swanson packets and used a little more lemon juice (1/3 cup instead of 1/4). Served it over rice. My family loved it! Thank you for sharing this.

I loved this recipe. I will cook the broccoli less next time. I didn't use lemon zest because I did not have an organic lemon. I used chicken breast because that is what I had on hand. The sauce was light and flavorful.

I was actually quite surprised at how good and flavorful this recipe was. And it's very healthy. I didn't have the concentrate broth packets so I just made a very concentrated broth w/ buillion cubes. I overcooked the chicken but that was my own fault. I needed to reduce the cooking time due to using boneless skinless chicken that I had butterflied.
Easy, lowfat and tasty main course. We loved the lemony taste of the chicken but next time would cut back on the onions and add mushrooms. Served over pasta

I put my chicken in cold--half frozen in fact--initially. This made the outside burnt which was a factor in the final dish. I think I put too much broth in as well. It wasn't easy figuring this ratio out because I had none of the concentrated broth and had to use buillon. It seems like the recipe could've taken into account the fact that bouillon is a lot more affordable to most people--or at least given a substitute ratio for the buillon. By the time this was finished, it was greasy, overcooked, and bitter. Again I bear a great deal of responsibility for this. I don't know if I would try this again. And I really was looking forward to something different. My husband hated it. A lot of trouble for nothing. Sorry.

Quick, easy and healthy! Surprisingly great flavour (I added a bit of lemon pepper but would still be good without). Served this with egg noodles. I dish supper with few calories and little clean up. Thanks so much to the submitter!
everyone loved this!
I made it

We found this to be just OK. I used BLSL breasts cut in strips. It was easy enough but just not very flavorful. There are better Lemon Chicken recipes out there. Thanks for the recipe but I'm not likely to make this one again.

We really liked the lemon flavor! I made as directed, except I only used 3 chicken breasts. And I didn't add any more olive oil when I sauteed the onions, I just took the chicken breasts out and threw the onions right into the pan.
We didn't care for this at all, we thought it lacked flavor. Will not make again.
I used chicken stock and thickened it at the end of cooking with corn starch. Yum!
